response.passage: Have you ever wondered how we see the world around us? We see objects because light reflects off them and enters our eyes, not because our eyes emit light. When you stand in front of a plane mirror, you see an image that appears to be behind the glass. This is a virtual image, which is perfectly visible to the human eye even though it cannot be caught on a screen. As you move further away from the mirror, your image remains the same size, though it appears to be at a greater distance. Interestingly, if you raise your right hand, the mirror image raises its left hand; this phenomenon is called lateral inversion, meaning the left and right sides are swapped, not the top and bottom. Many people mistakenly think lenses always magnify objects, but lenses are simply tools to bend light to form images. For example, some lenses make images smaller, while others make them larger. Similarly, mirrors like the convex mirrors on cars are used because they provide a wider field of view, allowing us to see more traffic behind us, rather than just making objects look bigger.
response.summary: We see objects through reflected light, and mirrors create virtual images that show lateral inversion. Lenses and mirrors serve various purposes beyond simple magnification, such as providing wider views or forming images at different sizes.
